s1.syndrome_frame: Multiple bluish, partially keratotic skin lesions with slow growth, associated with neurological deficits and family history of similar conditions
salient_findings: Multiple bluish, partially keratotic papules and nodules on the lower legs
key_facts: Female patient in her early 50s
Lesions on the lower legs have been growing slowly since age 24
Lesions have been bleeding occasionally after trauma
Patient uses a wheelchair due to right-sided hemiparesis and hemianopsia
Patient had recurrent seizures at age 4
Patient has lipolymphedema of the lower legs
Patient has been wearing compression stockings for years
Family history of similar conditions in the patient's father and aunt
Father died of an intracranial hemorrhage in his early 70s
Sonography demonstrated intradermal slow-flow vascular malformations
Histopathology revealed a well-circumscribed lesion with hyperkeratosis and acanthosis
Genetic testing detected a heterozygous pathogenic KRIT1 variant

shortlist.label: Cerebral Cavernous Malformations (CCM)
shortlist.why_kept: Detection of a heterozygous pathogenic KRIT1 variant and family history of similar conditions

shortlist.label: Familial cerebral cavernous malformations
shortlist.why_kept: Family history of similar conditions and presence of cerebral cavernous malformations

shortlist.label: Glomuvenous Malformation
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of venous malformations and family history of similar conditions

shortlist.label: Venous Malformation with Glomuvenous Malformation
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of venous malformations and family history of similar conditions

shortlist.label: Capillary Malformation-Arteriovenous Malformation Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of multiple bluish skin lesions and neurological deficits

raw.rationale: The patient's family history of similar conditions, including the father's death from an intracranial hemorrhage, combined with the detection of a heterozygous pathogenic KRIT1 variant, supports this diagnosis. The KRIT1 gene is associated with familial cerebral cavernous malformations.

rejected.label: Cerebral Cavernous Malformations (CCM)
rejected.why: While CCM is a possible diagnosis, the familial component and genetic testing results make familial cerebral cavernous malformations a more specific and accurate diagnosis.

rejected.label: Glomuvenous Malformation
rejected.why: The sonography and histopathology results do not specifically indicate glomuvenous malformation, and the genetic testing points towards a different condition.

rejected.label: Venous Malformation with Glomuvenous Malformation
rejected.why: The presence of intradermal slow-flow vascular malformations and the patient's symptoms could suggest a venous malformation, but the genetic testing and family history suggest a different primary diagnosis.

rejected.label: Capillary Malformation-Arteriovenous Malformation Syndrome
rejected.why: There is no indication of capillary malformations or arteriovenous malformations in the provided information, making this diagnosis less likely.
